# Task: fix a reported bug in `radix`

## Bug report (verbatim from the project's issue tracker)
**installHook.js:1 Error: Maximum update depth exceeded - React 19 + Radix**

## Bug report

### Current Behavior

When using Radix components with React 19, an infinite loop occurs causing the error:                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Error: Maximum update depth exceeded. This can happen when a component repeatedly calls setState inside componentWillUpdate or componentDidUpdate. React limits the number of  
  nested updates to prevent infinite loops.                                                                                                                                      
      at setRef (composeRefs.tsx:11:5)                                                                                                                                           
      at composeRefs.tsx:22:45                                                                                                                                                   
      at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)                                                                                                                                             
      at composeRefs.tsx:22:28                                                                                                                                                   
      at setRef (composeRefs.tsx:11:5)                                                                                                                                           
      at composeRefs.tsx:22:45                                                                                                                                                   
      ...                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  The setRef function in @radix-ui/react-compose-refs recursively triggers itself, causing React to hit the maximum update depth limit.                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  In React 19, ref callback behavior changed - ref callbacks can now return cleanup functions, and React may call ref callbacks differently than in React 18. When setRef calls  
  ref(value) at line 11, it triggers a re-render which invokes setRef again via the composed ref callback at line 22, creating an infinite loop.    


### Expected behavior

  Composed refs should work without causing infinite update loops in React 19.                                                                                                    

### Reproducible example

I have platejs plugins with radix popovers and radix tooltips on them. If I write fast inside plate, the page breaks. 
I'm on a Macbook M1 Pro with 32 GB. One way to trigger this error is to inspect chrome and start a performance recording and start typing real fast. On Safari, for example, it doesn't break. I tried on restarted browser, guest mode. I'm not the only one

[CodeSandbox Template](n/a)

### Suggested solution

  The composeRefs and useComposedRefs functions need to handle React 19's new ref callback behavior. Possible approaches:                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  1. Memoize the composed ref callback to prevent unnecessary re-invocations                                                                                                     
  2. Add a guard to prevent recursive setRef calls                                                                                                                               
  3. Handle the cleanup function return value from React 19 ref callbacks       

### Additional context
Right now, it works fine with react 18 (even on next.js 16+) and we had to downgrade.

I also saw this reddit post https://www.reddit.com/r/react/comments/1nnvwsp/react_19_causes_maximum_update_depth_exceeded/ where a user raised a similar case

React 19 introduced changes to ref callback behavior, including support for cleanup functions returned from ref callbacks. This may be causing the ref to be re-invoked on each render cycle.                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Related stack trace also shows Slate editor involvement:                                                                                                                       
  at Slate.useCallback[onContextChange] (slate.tsx:62:7)                                                                                                                         
  at e.onChange (with-dom.ts:371:7)                                                                                                                                              
  at with-react.ts:54:7                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  This suggests the issue manifests when Radix components are used alongside Slate/Plate editors, where both libraries compose refs. 

### Your environment

| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-compose-refs          | 1.1.0         |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-accordion             | 1.2.12        |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-avatar                | 1.1.11        |

  - Next.js: 16.1.1

  - platejs: 52.0.15

Do not ask me for permission between steps; proceed until the task is complete, then report.

Re-render creates another new `composeRefs` → goto 1\r\n  4. \"Maximum update depth exceeded\"\r\n\r\n  ## Solution\r\n\r\n  Memoize the composed ref via `React.useMemo` so the ref identity stays stable across renders. The memoization depends on `forwardedRef` and `childrenRef` — it only recomputes\r\n  when the actual refs change, not on every render.\r\n\r\n  ## How this differs from #3804\r\n\r\n  PR #3804 switches to `useComposedRefs`, but comments there note that `useComposedRefs` itself is unstable when callers pass inline arrow functions. This approach memoizes\r\n  directly at the call site in `SlotClone`, which is the minimal change needed — it keeps `composeRefs` untouched and just stabilizes the ref identity where it matters.\r\n\r\n  ## Validation\r\n\r\n  Running in production on a large enterprise React 19 app since Feb 2026. Zero recurrence of the infinite loop across Tooltip, Select, Popover, and Dialog components.\r\n\r\n<!--\r\n\r\nThank you for contributing!       "body": "## Bug report\n\n### Current Behavior\n\nReact logs:\n\n```\nflushSync was called from inside a lifecycle method. React cannot flush when\nReact is already rendering. Consider moving this call to a scheduler task or micro task.\n```\n\nwhen a `Switch` or `Checkbox` **mounts inside a `<form>` while an open `Popover` is being dismissed by the same click**.\n\nStack trace is entirely Radix + React-DOM internals — no frames from application code:\n\n```\nexports.flushSync                                react-dom\ndispatchDiscreteCustomEvent                      @radix-ui\nhandleAndDispatchCustomEvent                     @radix-ui\nhandleAndDispatchPointerDownOutsideEvent         @radix-ui  — DismissableLayer outside-click detection\nSwitchBubbleInput.useEffect                      @radix-ui/react-switch\n… commitHookEffectListMount / commitPassiveMountOnFiber (×~140)\n```\n\n`SwitchBubbleInput` is the hidden native `<input>` that lets a Switch participate in real HTML forms. Its **mount effect** calls into the still-open Popover's outside-click dispatch, which calls `flushSync` — during a passive-effect commit. That is precisely what React's guard exists to catch.\n\nDev-only: React strips this diagnostic from production builds.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nNo warning. The dismissal dispatch should not run `flushSync` re-entrantly inside a passive-effect commit — deferring it to a microtask or scheduler task, as React's own message suggests, would presumably be enough.\n\n### Reproduction\n\n```tsx\n<form noValidate>\n  <Popover>\n    <PopoverTrigger>Open</PopoverTrigger>\n    <PopoverContent>{/* anything */}</PopoverContent>\n  </Popover>\n  <Switch />   {/* or Checkbox */}\n</form>\n```\n\n1. Open the popover.\n2. Click inside it.\n3. Click the `Switch`/`Checkbox` **without closing the popover first**, so the click is handled as outside-click dismissal.\n\n### What isolates it\n\nSix reproductions, each removing one variable. The deciding pair is 5 vs 6:\n\n| # | Contents | Reproduces |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Bare `Popover` + `Switch`/`Checkbox`, `useState`, **no form** | No |\n| 2 | Same, with a real date-picker calendar inside the popover | No |\n| 3 | Same, wired through `react-hook-form`'s `Controller` | No |\n| 4 | A real 3-field form (`date` + `switch` + `checkbox`) | **Yes** |\n| 5 | The same field renderers, hand-composed, **no `<form>`** | No |\n| 6 | The same renderers in a **bare `<form noValidate>`** — no form library, no context, no providers | **Yes** |\n\n**A native `<form>` ancestor is the trigger, and nothing else is.** Not the date picker (2, 3 used a real calendar), not `react-hook-form` (3), not tree size or field count, not any form-library context (6 has none).\n\nIt also requires the popover to be **still open when the click lands** — dismiss-by-click, not dismiss-by-Escape. Escape-then-click never reproduced. And it is **not Switch-specific**: `Checkbox` behaves identically, which fits, since `CheckboxBubbleInput` is the same pattern.\n\n### Suggested cause\n\nThe `BubbleInput` components are the form-aware part, which is consistent with a `<form>` ancestor being the trigger — plausibly a `closest(\"form\")` check or a native reset/submit listener changing effect timing. **Stated as a hypothesis, not a finding:** we did not read the unminified source to confirm *why* the form ancestor unlocks it, only that it reliably does.\n\n### Not tested\n\nWhether `Dialog` / `DropdownMenu` fire it too. All three share `DismissableLayer`, so they plausibly do — this issue names `Popover` because that is where we hit it.\n\n### Prior art checked\n\n- #2549 \"[Checkbox] Controlled Checkbox inside a form will trigger an infinite loop\" — same *\"inside a form\"* trigger, different symptom (`Maximum update depth exceeded`, not `flushSync`), and closed.\n- #4014 \"[DismissableLayer] Escape handlers go stale on React 19.2\" — same subsystem, different failure.\n\nNeither looks like a duplicate, but happy to be pointed at one if this is already tracked.\n\n### Context\n\nFound while maintaining a component library built on Radix. There is no fix available on our side: the stack contains none of our code, and the behaviour is internal to the dismissal dispatch. Reporting rather than working around it, since a workaround here would mean reaching into internals with no version guarantee.",

      "body": "### Description\n\n**Fixes [#3858](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives/issues/3858)**\n\n`PopperAnchor` has a `useEffect` with **no dependency array** that calls `context.onAnchorChange()` (which is `setState`) on every render. React calls callback refs during DOM attachment in the commit phase, which does not count toward the nested update limit. The `useEffect` is kept only for the `virtualRef` case (non-DOM anchors like pointer positions).\n\n### Verified\n\nThe fix was verified via `pnpm patch` on `@radix-ui/react-popper@1.2.7` by the original reporter. A page with 60+ Radix Tooltip components no longer throws \"Maximum update depth exceeded\" on initial render.\n",

      "body": "## Bug report\n\n### Current behavior\n\n`PopperAnchor` has a `useEffect` with **no dependency array** that calls `context.onAnchorChange()` (which is `setState`) on every render:\n\n```jsx\nReact.useEffect(() => {\n  context.onAnchorChange(virtualRef?.current || ref.current);\n}); // ← no dependency array\n```\n\nWhen a page has 50+ Radix components that use Popper internally (Tooltip, Popover, DropdownMenu, HoverCard), each `PopperAnchor` calls `setState` during the passive effects phase on mount. React counts all of these against a **single 50-update limit per commit cycle**, causing:\n\n```\nError: Maximum update depth exceeded. This can happen when a component\nrepeatedly calls setState inside componentWillUpdate or componentDidUpdate.\nReact limits the number of nested updates to prevent infinite loops.\n```\n\nThis is **not** an infinite loop — it's a cumulative depth issue from too many independent Popper instances mounting simultaneously. React Strict Mode (which double-invokes effects) makes this worse in development.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\n`PopperAnchor` should not contribute to React's nested update depth counter on mount. The anchor element only needs to be set once when the DOM node is attached.\n\n### Proposed fix\n\nReplace the dependency-less `useEffect` + `setState` with a **callback ref**:\n\n```jsx\nconst callbackRef = React.useCallback((node) => {\n  ref.current = node;\n  if (node) context.onAnchorChange(node);\n}, [context.onAnchorChange]);\nconst composedRefs = useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, virtualRef ? ref : callbackRef);\nReact.useEffect(() => {\n  if (virtualRef?.current) context.onAnchorChange(virtualRef.current);\n}, [virtualRef, context.onAnchorChange]);\n```\n\nReact calls callback refs during DOM attachment in the commit phase, which **does not count** toward the nested update limit. The `useEffect` is kept only for the `virtualRef` case.\n\nWe verified this fix works via a `pnpm patch` on `@radix-ui/react-popper@1.2.7`.\n\n### Reproduction\n\nAny page with 50+ Radix Tooltip/Popover/DropdownMenu/HoverCard components mounting in a single render pass. In our case: a workbench page with a sidebar nav (~10 items with Tooltips), action buttons with Tooltips (~15), and an inline document editor with citation HoverCards (~30+).\n\n### Environment\n\n- `@radix-ui/react-popper`: 1.2.7\n- React 19.2.3\n- Verified in both development (StrictMode) and production builds\n\n### Your minimal, reproducible example\n\nMount 60 Radix Tooltip components in a single page. Observe \"Maximum update depth exceeded\" on initial render.\n\n### Relevant package versions\n\n- `@radix-ui/react-tooltip`: 1.2.7\n- `@radix-ui/react-popper`: 1.2.7\n- `react`: 19.2.3\n- `react-dom`: 19.2.3",

      "body": "### Summary\n\n#3899 fixed the React 19 infinite re-render loop in `Slot` by stabilizing its composed ref (released in `react-slot@1.2.5`, closing #3799). The same unstable-identity pattern still exists in several other packages' own code, and under React 19's ref-cleanup semantics each of them reproduces the exact same `Maximum update depth exceeded` crash.\n\n### Mechanism\n\n`useComposedRefs` is `React.useCallback(composeRefs(...refs), refs)`. When any member of `refs` is an inline arrow function (or the composition is done with a bare `composeRefs(...)` call in render), the composed callback gets a new identity every render. React 19 then detaches and re-attaches the ref on every commit; any composed state-setter ref toggles its state `null -> node` each cycle, which schedules another render, which produces another new identity - an infinite loop that ends in `Maximum update depth exceeded`.\n\nTypical stack:\n\n```\ndispatchSetState\nsetRef            (@radix-ui/react-compose-refs)\nArray.map         (composeRefs)\nsetRef            (outer composition re-firing the inner one)\n```\n\n### Affected sites (verified against the latest published versions, June 2026)\n\n| Package | Site | Unstable member |\n|---|---|---|\n| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectContentImpl` | `(node) => setContent(node)` |\n| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectItemAlignedPosition` | `(node) => setContent(node)` |\n| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectItem` | `(node) => contentContext.itemRefCallback?.(node, value, disabled)` |\n| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectItemText` | `(node) => setItemTextNode(node)` and `(node) => contentContext.itemTextRefCallback?.(...)` |\n| `react-dropdown-menu@2.1.17` | `DropdownMenuTrigger` | render-inline `ref: composeRefs(forwardedRef, context.triggerRef)` |\n| `react-menu@2.1.17` | `MenuSubTrigger` | render-inline `ref: composeRefs(forwardedRef, subContext.onTriggerChange)` (composed directly with a state setter) |\n| `react-popper@1.3.0` | `PopperContent` | `(node) => setContent(node)` |\n| `react-focus-scope@1.1.9` | `FocusScope` | `(node) => setContainer(node)` |\n| `react-dismissable-layer@1.1.12` | `DismissableLayer` | `(node2) => setNode(node2)` |\n| `react-scroll-area@1.2.11` | `ScrollArea` / `Scrollbar` / `Thumb` | `(node) => setScrollArea(node)`, `(node) => setScrollbar(node)`, `(node) => scrollbarContext.onThumbChange(node)` |\n\n`react-dismissable-layer` deserves emphasis: it wraps every menu/popover/dialog content stack, so after patching the others it remained the residual loop driver in our app.\n\n### Real-world impact\n\nReact 19.2.3 SPA (Vite). Intermittent full-page crashes (caught by our ErrorBoundary) on any page with an open Select/DropdownMenu/Popover - a few percent of page loads in production, and frequent enough under parallel E2E load to fail CI on most runs. After stabilizing all the sites above (local `pnpm patch`es), the crash is gone across thousands of E2E test executions: before the patches we reproduced it reliably; after, zero occurrences.\n\n### Suggested fix (same principle as #3899)\n\n- Pass state setters directly: `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, setContent)` - identical semantics, stable identity.\n- Wrap closures that capture per-render values in `useCallbackRef` before composing.\n- Hoist render-inline `composeRefs(...)` calls (dropdown-menu trigger, menu sub-trigger) into `useComposedRefs` above the JSX.\n\nWe run all of these as local patches today and they are mechanical; happy to turn them into a PR if useful.\n\n### Environment\n\n- React / react-dom 19.2.3\n- @radix-ui packages at the versions listed above (all latest stable as of June 12, 2026)\n- Reproduces in Chromium (Playwright) and real Chrome; intermittent, load/timing dependent",

65:      "body": "… in React 19

Fixes #3799

  ## Problem

  In `SlotClone`, `composeRefs(forwardedRef, childrenRef)` is called inline during render, creating a new function identity on every render. In React 19, ref identity changes
  trigger ref cleanup + re-attach. When a state setter is used as a ref (e.g., Tooltip's `setTrigger`), this causes an infinite loop:

  1. New `composeRefs` → React detects ref identity change
  2. React calls cleanup (`setTrigger(null)`) → state update → re-render
  3. Re-render creates another new `composeRefs` → goto 1
  4. "Maximum update depth exceeded"

  ## Solution

  Memoize the composed ref via `React.useMemo` so the ref identity stays stable across renders. The memoization depends on `forwardedRef` and `childrenRef` — it only recomputes
  when the actual refs change, not on every render.

  ## How this differs from #3804

  PR #3804 switches to `useComposedRefs`, but comments there note that `useComposedRefs` itself is unstable when callers pass inline arrow functions. This approach memoizes
  directly at the call site in `SlotClone`, which is the minimal change needed — it keeps `composeRefs` untouched and just stabilizes the ref identity where it matters.

  ## Validation

  Running in production on a large enterprise React 19 app since Feb 2026. Zero recurrence of the infinite loop across Tooltip, Select, Popover, and Dialog components.

The same unstable-identity pattern still exists in several other packages' own code, and under React 19's ref-cleanup semantics each of them reproduces the exact same `Maximum update depth exceeded` crash.

### Mechanism

`useComposedRefs` is `React.useCallback(composeRefs(...refs), refs)`. When any member of `refs` is an inline arrow function (or the composition is done with a bare `composeRefs(...)` call in render), the composed callback gets a new identity every render. React 19 then detaches and re-attaches the ref on every commit; any composed state-setter ref toggles its state `null -> node` each cycle, which schedules another render, which produces another new identity - an infinite loop that ends in `Maximum update depth exceeded`.

Typical stack:

```
dispatchSetState
setRef            (@radix-ui/react-compose-refs)
Array.map         (composeRefs)
setRef            (outer composition re-firing the inner one)
```

### Affected sites (verified against the latest published versions, June 2026)

| Package | Site | Unstable member |
|---|---|---|
| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectContentImpl` | `(node) => setContent(node)` |
| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectItemAlignedPosition` | `(node) => setContent(node)` |
| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectItem` | `(node) => contentContext.itemRefCallback?.(node, value, disabled)` |
| `react-select@2.3.0` | `SelectItemText` | `(node) => setItemTextNode(node)` and `(node) => contentContext.itemTextRefCallback?.(...)` |
| `react-dropdown-menu@2.1.17` | `DropdownMenuTrigger` | render-inline `ref: composeRefs(forwardedRef, context.triggerRef)` |
| `react-menu@2.1.17` | `MenuSubTrigger` | render-inline `ref: composeRefs(forwardedRef, subContext.onTriggerChange)` (composed directly with a state setter) |
| `react-popper@1.3.0` | `PopperContent` | `(node) => setContent(node)` |
| `react-focus-scope@1.1.9` | `FocusScope` | `(node) => setContainer(node)` |
| `react-dismissable-layer@1.1.12` | `DismissableLayer` | `(node2) => setNode(node2)` |
| `react-scroll-area@1.2.11` | `ScrollArea` / `Scrollbar` / `Thumb` | `(node) => setScrollArea(node)`, `(node) => setScrollbar(node)`, `(node) => scrollbarContext.onThumbChange(node)` |

`react-dismissable-layer` deserves emphasis: it wraps every menu/popover/dialog content stack, so after patching the others it remained the residual loop driver in our app.

### Real-world impact

React 19.2.3 SPA (Vite). Intermittent full-page crashes (caught by our ErrorBoundary) on any page with an open Select/DropdownMenu/Popover - a few percent of page loads in production, and frequent enough under parallel E2E load to fail CI on most runs. After stabilizing all the sites above (local `pnpm patch`es), the crash is gone across thousands of E2E test executions: before the patches we reproduced it reliably; after, zero occurrences.

### Suggested fix (same principle as #3899)

- Pass state setters directly: `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, setContent)` - identical semantics, stable identity.
- Wrap closures that capture per-render values in `useCallbackRef` before composing.
- Hoist render-inline `composeRefs(...)` calls (dropdown-menu trigger, menu sub-trigger) into `useComposedRefs` above the JSX.

We run all of these as local patches today and they are mechanical; happy to turn them into a PR if useful.

### Environment

- React / react-dom 19.2.3
- @radix-ui packages at the versions listed above (all latest stable as of June 12, 2026)
- Reproduces in Chromium (Playwright) and real Chrome; intermittent, load/timing dependent",

Fixes #3799

  ## Problem

  In `SlotClone`, `composeRefs(forwardedRef, childrenRef)` is called inline during render, creating a new function identity on every render. In React 19, ref identity changes
  trigger ref cleanup + re-attach. When a state setter is used as a ref (e.g., Tooltip's `setTrigger`), this causes an infinite loop:

  2. React calls cleanup (`setTrigger(null)`) → state update → re-render
  3. Re-render creates another new `composeRefs` → goto 1
  4. "Maximum update depth exceeded"

Now I understand the official fix. The root cause is:

In `Slot`, `composeRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)` is called inline during render, creating a new function identity on every render. In React 19, ref identity changes trigger ref cleanup + re-attach. When a state setter is used as a ref (e.g., Tooltip's `setTrigger`), this causes an infinite loop:
1. New `composeRefs` → React detects ref identity change
2. React calls cleanup (`setTrigger(null)`) → state update → re-render
3. Re-render creates another new `composeRefs` → goto 1
4. "Maximum update depth exceeded"

The fix uses `useComposedRefs` which memoizes the composed ref via `React.useCallback`.

But wait — the fix moves `getElementRef(slottableElement)` and `useComposedRefs` BEFORE the `if (!slottableElement)` check. Hmm, but `useComposedRefs` is a hook, so it must be called unconditionally (not conditionally). That's why the fix moves it before the early return. And `slottableElementRef` becomes `undefined` when there's no slottable element — `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, undefined)` handles that fine.

Now, note the current repo's `slot.tsx` already has a different structure (it uses the newer `createSlot` refactoring from #3729 with `createSlot(ownerName)`). The current version already calls `useComposedRefs`... wait, let me re-read the current slot.tsx.

Current slot.tsx line 74-75:
```js
const slottableElementRef = getElementRef(slottableElement);
const composedRefs = composeRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef);
```

So the current repo uses `composeRefs` (not `useComposedRefs`) and calls it after the `if (!slottableElement)` early return. The fix should:
1. Move `slottableElementRef` and `composedRef` computation before the `if (!slottableElement)` block (to satisfy rules of hooks since `useComposedRefs` is a hook)
2. Use `useComposedRefs` instead of `composeRefs`

But wait — the current slot.tsx has the `if (!slottableElement)` early return at line 62-72, and `getElementRef` at line 74. If I use `useComposedRefs`, I MUST call it before the early return (hooks can't be conditional). So I need to move the `getElementRef` call and `useComposedRefs` call above the `if (!slottableElement)` block.

Now, there's a subtlety with the current `createSlot` structure: the `Slot` function uses `React.forwardRef`. Calling hooks inside the forwardRef render is fine.

Let me verify the current state of slot.tsx and apply the fix. But first, let me also reproduce the bug to make sure my understanding is right. The bug requires a ref that triggers a state update (like a state setter) to cause the infinite loop.

Let me write a better reproduction that actually reproduces the infinite loop. In the official test, they use:
```jsx
const ref = React.useCallback((node) => { if (node) forceRender(); }, []);
return (
  <Slot ref={ref}>
    <button type="button">Click me</button>
  </Slot>
);
```

Wait but that ref is stable (useCallback with []). So why would that cause an infinite loop with composeRefs? Because the child is a `<button>` with no ref. So `slottableElementRef = getElementRef(slottableElement)` is undefined. Then `composeRefs(forwardedRef, undefined)` is created fresh each render. The composed ref identity changes each render → React 19 calls cleanup + re-attach on each render. The cleanup calls `setRef(refs[1]=undefined, null)` — no-op, and `setRef(refs[0]=ref, null)` → calls `ref(null)` → no forceRender. Then re-attach calls `ref(node)` → `forceRender()` → re-render → new composed ref → cleanup → re-attach → forceRender → infinite loop.

Yes! So the reproduction is: a stable ref that forces a re-render, combined with the composed ref getting a new identity each render because `composeRefs` is called inline.

Done. Summary:

## Root cause
`Slot` in `packages/react/slot/src/slot.tsx` called `composeRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)` **inline during render**, creating a brand-new composed ref callback with a new identity on **every** render.

In React 19, when a ref's identity changes, React runs the previous ref's cleanup and re-attaches the ref on every commit. When one of the composed refs triggers a state update (e.g. a state setter used as a ref, like Tooltip's `setTrigger`), that update re-renders `Slot`, which creates another new composed-ref identity, which detaches/re-attaches again, firing the setter again → infinite loop → "Maximum update depth exceeded" (issue #3799). React 18 didn't loop because it didn't re-attach refs on identity change.

## Changes
- `packages/react/slot/src/slot.tsx:2,62-63,81` — replaced `composeRefs(...)` with `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)`, which memoizes the composed ref via `useCallback` so its identity is stable across renders. Moved the `getElementRef`/`useComposedRefs` call above the `!slottableElement` early-return to keep the hook unconditional (rules of hooks).
- `packages/react/slot/src/slot-ref-stability.test.tsx` (new) — regression tests: (1) attaching a ref that triggers a render no longer causes an infinite loop, (2) the composed ref passed to the child has a stable identity across re-renders.
- `packages/react/slot/src/slot.test.tsx` — un-skipped the previously-disabled "given an Input" suite (same underlying issue, related to #3554); it now passes.
- `.changeset/slot-ref-stability.md` (new) — changeset patch entry.

## Verification
- Reproduced first: wrote a failing test hitting `Maximum update depth exceeded` on the unpatched code (failed), then passed after the fix.
- `pnpm vitest run packages/react/slot` → 2 files / 33 tests pass; `oxlint` lint and `tsc --noEmit` typecheck both clean.

There's a type error in the typecheck. The issue is `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, subContext.onTriggerChange)` — `subContext.onTriggerChange` is `(trigger: MenuSubTriggerElement | null) => void`. And `useComposedRefs<T>` infers T from the refs. The error: `Type 'HTMLDivElement | null' is not assignable to type '((prevState: null) => null) | null'`. 

This suggests `useComposedRefs` is inferring the ref type from `forwardedRef` — forwardedRef is `React.ForwardedRef<MenuSubTriggerElement>` which is `HTMLDivElement | null | ...`. And `onTriggerChange` is typed as `(trigger: MenuSubTriggerElement | null) => void`. 

The problem is that `onTriggerChange` when treated as a `React.Ref<T>`... A function `(trigger: MenuSubTriggerElement | null) => void` is assignable to `RefCallback<MenuSubTriggerElement>`? `RefCallback<T> = (instance: T | null) => void`. So `onTriggerChange` matches `RefCallback<MenuSubTriggerElement>`. And `forwardedRef: ForwardedRef<MenuSubTriggerElement>` also matches. So T should unify to `MenuSubTriggerElement`.

But the error mentions `((prevState: null) => null) | null` — that's the type of `setTrigger`! Wait no, `onTriggerChange={setTrigger}`. `setTrigger` is `Dispatch<SetStateAction<MenuSubTriggerElement | null>>`. That's `(value: SetStateAction<MenuSubTriggerElement | null>) => void` which is `(value: MenuSubTriggerElement | null | ((prevState) => ...)) => void`. So `onTriggerChange` accepts a broader type.

When `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, onTriggerChange)` — TypeScript infers T. `forwardedRef` is `ForwardedRef<MenuSubTriggerElement>`. For `useComposedRefs<T>(...refs: PossibleRef<T>[])` where `PossibleRef<T> = React.Ref<T> | undefined`. `React.Ref<T> = RefCallback<T> | RefObject<T> | null`. So `forwardedRef` → T = MenuSubTriggerElement. Then `onTriggerChange` must be `RefCallback<MenuSubTriggerElement> = (instance: MenuSubTriggerElement | null) => void`. But `onTriggerChange` is `(trigger: MenuSubTriggerElement | null) => void`... that should match.

Wait the error says the inferred type becomes `((prevState: null) => null) | null`. Hmm, that means TS inferred T such that the ref type becomes the setter's functional update form. This is a known TS inference issue with `useComposedRefs` when a setter is passed — the setter's parameter is a union `T | ((prevState: T) => T)` and TS picks the wrong inference.

But wait — the existing code in menu.tsx line 385: `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, contentRef, context.onContentChange)` — this works with a setter. And in `MenuSubContent` line 1179: `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, ref)`. And in NavigationMenu line 119: `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, (node) => setNavigationMenu(node))` — wrapping the setter in an arrow to avoid the inference problem!

So the workaround used elsewhere is to wrap the setter in a callback. But `setTrigger` is not a setter directly — `onTriggerChange` is a function type `(trigger: ...) => void`. parts.text:
Report on the pattern elsewhere in `packages/react`:

**Found 3 render-inline `composeRefs(...)` call sites (the same unstable-identity pattern):**

| File | Line | Ref members | Same bug? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `menu.tsx` `MenuSubTrigger` | 1056 | `forwardedRef` + `subContext.onTriggerChange` (= `setTrigger` state setter) | **Yes** — reproduced (see below) |
| `dropdown-menu.tsx` `DropdownMenuTrigger` | 116 | `forwardedRef` + `context.triggerRef` (ref object) | **Yes** — reproduced |
| `navigation-menu.tsx` `NavigationMenuViewport` | 1081 | `ref` (item) + `(node) => { if (isActive && node) setContent(node); }` | **No** — `setContent` is guarded by `isActive && node` and React bails when the node is unchanged, so it can't loop. Also it's inside a `.map()`, so `useComposedRefs` can't be hoisted without a larger refactor. |

## What I fixed (the two "same bug" sites)

Both `menu.tsx` and `dropdown-menu.tsx` hoisted the inline `composeRefs(...)` into `useComposedRefs(...)`, which memoizes the composed ref so its identity is stable across renders (same principle as the Slot fix). The member refs are the same — behavior preserved; only the identity is stabilized.

## Verification

- Wrote `menu-ref-stability.test.tsx` and `dropdown-menu-ref-stability.test.tsx`; both failed with `Maximum update depth exceeded` on the original code and pass after the fix (confirmed each by temporarily reverting).
- `pnpm vitest run packages/react/slot packages/react/menu packages/react/dropdown-menu` → 4 files / 36 tests pass.
- `oxlint` and `tsc --noEmit` clean for all three packages.
- Added changesets for `@radix-ui/react-menu` and `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu` (patch), alongside the existing slot one.

Files changed: `packages/react/menu/src/menu.tsx`, `packages/react/dropdown-menu/src/dropdown-menu.tsx`, plus the two new regression test files and two changesets. `navigation-menu` left untouched (not the same bug).
